title: Operating an Elasticsearch Log Cluster
intro: In an ELK/EFK stack, Elasticsearch stores and searches the logs. When log search gets slow or stops ingesting, these are the calls you'll make first.

steps.explanation: green = all shards assigned; yellow = all primaries assigned but some replicas aren't; red = some primary data is unavailable.
steps.why: Yellow means no data loss yet, but you've lost redundancy — one more node failure could turn it red. Always check why shards are unassigned.

steps.prompt: List all indices with their size and document counts.
steps.fake_output:
health status index              docs.count  store.size
yellow open   logs-2026.09.27    48210931    38.1gb
green  open   logs-2026.09.26    51002110    40.2gb
green  open   logs-2026.06.01    39120001    31.0gb
steps.explanation: One index per day — including a logs-2026.06.01 that's almost four months old.
steps.why: Daily indices make retention easy: deleting old days is cheap. Keeping months of verbose logs is a common reason clusters run out of disk.
The q= query-string search is quick for ad-hoc checks from a terminal; Kibana's KQL (service:"payments-api" and message:timeout) is the everyday interface for humans.

steps.prompt: Check disk usage per node — Elasticsearch stops allocating shards when disks fill past its watermarks.
steps.fake_output:
shards disk.used disk.avail disk.percent node
   140     456gb       44gb           91 es-node-1
   138     401gb       99gb           80 es-node-2
steps.explanation: es-node-1 is at 91% — past the default 90% high watermark, so ES is moving shards off it and won't put new ones there.
steps.why: That's why shards were unassigned (yellow). At 95% (the flood-stage watermark) ES makes indices READ-ONLY, and log ingestion stops entirely (see monitoring-incident-004).

steps.prompt: Delete the ancient logs-2026.06.01 index to free space.
steps.why: Irreversible — double-check the exact index name first, and never use wildcards casually here. Index Lifecycle Management (ILM) automates this so nobody has to run deletes by hand.
